channel.title: Cadence Evidence — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 56 sources.

item.title: Is Reduced Spinal Range of Motion a Prognostic Factor for Pain Intensity, Disability, and Global Recovery in People With Specific or Nonspecific Spinal Pain? A Systematic Review.
item.description: A systematic review of 37 studies found very low certainty evidence regarding whether reduced spinal range of motion is a prognostic factor for pain, disability, or recovery in spinal pain patients, with inconsistent results and all studies rated as high risk of bias.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effect of iTBS and rTMS Combined with Robotic Rehabilitation on Ambulation and Lower Extremity Motor Function in Chronic SCI Patients.
item.description: An RCT found that intermittent theta-burst stimulation (iTBS) and repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) combined with robotic rehabilitation improved ambulation and lower extremity motor function in chronic spinal cord injury patients compared to sham, with no significant differences between active protocols.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Shear wave elastography for assessing lower extremity muscle stiffness after anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction: A systematic review.
item.description: A systematic review concluded that shear wave elastography can detect muscle-specific stiffness deficits after ACL reconstruction, including reduced vastus medialis and semitendinosus stiffness, which correlate with function beyond strength, but standardized protocols are required for clinical guidance.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: A Return to Performance Continuum for Football (Soccer) Players After ACL Reconstruction: Bridging Rehabilitation, Return to Play and Sustained Performance.
item.description: A paper outlines a staged Return to Performance continuum for football players after ACL reconstruction, bridging rehabilitation and sustained performance. It emphasizes restoring movement quality, progressive football-specific technical/tactical retraining, physical reconditioning, and maximal strength restoration.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Association Between Early Postoperative Limb Symmetry Index Scores and 2-Year Patient-Reported Outcomes After Quadriceps Tendon Autograft ACL Reconstruction.
item.description: A case series of 100 patients undergoing QT-ACLR showed that early isometric quadriceps LSI at 3 months (β = 3.9; adjusted R² = 0.36; P < .03) and isokinetic quadriceps strength at 9 months (β = 3.9-4.7; adjusted R² = 0.34-0.35; P ≤ .003) were independently associated with higher 2-year IKDC and Lysholm scores.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Post burn Cubital Tunnel Syndrome Electrophysiological and Functional Responses to High intensity Laser Therapy versus Extracorporeal Shock Wave Therapy: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial (N=75) found that both high-intensity laser therapy (HILT) and extracorporeal shock wave therapy (ESWT) combined with ulnar nerve gliding exercises (UNGE) improved nerve conduction and upper-limb function more than UNGE alone in post-burn cubital tunnel syndrome. HILT produced significantly greater improvements than ESWT in electrophysiological outcomes and DASH scores, with benefits maintained at 12-week follow-up (all P < .001).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Percutaneous Electrolysis for the Management of Musculoskeletal Disorders. A Systematic Review With Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis found very low-certainty evidence that adding percutaneous electrolysis (PNE) to therapeutic exercise (TE) was not superior to sham or TE alone for pain or function in tendinopathies. Low-certainty evidence showed PNE plus TE provided greater short- to medium-term pain reduction compared to dry needling plus TE in tendinopathies, but no significant differences in myofascial pain syndrome.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: The effects of route previewing on adaptive gait and gaze behaviour under cognitive dual-task conditions in older adults
item.description: This study found that cognitive dual-tasking increased stepping errors and reduced stride length, but route previewing significantly mitigated these negative effects on adaptive gait and gaze behavior. Previewing prior to gait initiation helped participants look further ahead and make fewer irrelevant fixations, improving walking safety under cognitive load.
item.author: medRxiv

item.title: Can Psychological Readiness Predict Successful Return to Sports After Patellar Stabilization Surgery in Adolescent Patients? A Retrospective Cohort Study.
item.description: A retrospective cohort study of 97 adolescent patients found that ACL-RSI scores ≥59.2 were associated with a 3.56 times increased likelihood of successful return to sport (78.3% overall) after patellar stabilization surgery, independently of sex, procedure type, or injury characteristics.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effectiveness of office-based vergence/accommodative therapy with movement for accommodative dysfunction in concussion-related convergence insufficiency: a secondary analysis of the CONCUSS randomised clinical trial
item.description: A secondary analysis of the CONCUSS RCT found that 12 sessions of immediate office-based vergence/accommodative therapy with movement (OBVAM) and home reinforcement remediated 86% of accommodative dysfunction in concussion-related convergence insufficiency, compared to 28% in the watchful waiting group.
item.author: BJSM

item.title: Efficacy and evidence certainty of traditional Chinese exercises for musculoskeletal disorders: an umbrella review of meta-analyses
item.description: An umbrella review synthesizing 547 unique associations from meta-analyses established high-certainty evidence for traditional Chinese exercises (TCEs), especially Tai Chi, in improving physical function in knee osteoarthritis, mental health in neck pain, and sleep quality in fibromyalgia. Optimal benefits were achieved with sustained interventions of ≥6 months duration, ≥3 times/week frequency, and ≥150 min weekly volume.
item.author: BJSM

item.title: Dextrose prolotherapy for chronic symptomatic rotator cuff tendinopathy and subacromial bursitis: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 14 studies found very low certainty evidence that dextrose prolotherapy offers little to no benefit for chronic rotator cuff tendinopathy/bursitis compared to saline, and may result in worse physical performance compared to corticosteroid injections.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Patients' experiences of participating in physiotherapeutic telerehabilitation for postpartum pelvic floor dysfunction; a qualitative study.
item.description: A qualitative study exploring patients' experiences with physiotherapeutic telerehabilitation for postpartum pelvic floor dysfunction found it was perceived as a complementary tool that improves accessibility and flexibility, but highlighted the need for advanced digital communication and concerns about the lack of physical examination.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: The enhanced rehabilitation programme for significant musculoskeletal injuries from the manchester arena bombing - A process evaluation study investigating patients' and physiotherapists' experiences.
item.description: A process evaluation of an enhanced rehabilitation program for major trauma survivors found it beneficial for recovery and motivation but identified challenges in sustaining progress and transitioning to standard care, indicating a need for improved long-term rehabilitation pathways.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: First aggression as a planning signal in post-acute stroke rehabilitation: Service benchmarks, goal setting, and a 60-day precaution window from a comprehensive observational cohort.
item.description: An observational study in post-acute stroke rehabilitation established service benchmarks following the first aggression event, indicating a 60-day precaution window and functional gaps to inform goal setting and discharge planning, though multicenter validation is needed.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Association between hospital-level factors and early rehabilitation initiation in patients with acute ischemic stroke: a multilevel analysis using a Japanese administrative database from a rural prefecture.
item.description: A multilevel analysis of Japanese administrative data revealed that hospital-level provision of weekend rehabilitation services was significantly associated with earlier initiation of rehabilitation for acute ischemic stroke patients.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: An exploration of self-evaluation of induced temporal and spatial gait asymmetry in neurotypical young adults.
item.description: This study found that neurotypical adults are more accurate in self-evaluating temporal gait asymmetry than spatial asymmetry, and focusing attention on the swing phase may enhance temporal self-evaluation, offering insights for post-stroke gait rehabilitation.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Quantifying Static Postural Control Impairment after Stroke using Markerless Motion Capture
item.description: Markerless motion capture effectively quantifies static postural control impairment in individuals with stroke, with parameters showing strong correlations to clinical balance measures, indicating its potential for clinical assessment.
item.author: medRxiv

item.title: Experiences of sexual rehabilitation post-stroke among LGBTQI+ stroke survivors and their partners: a qualitative study.
item.description: A qualitative study explored the sexual rehabilitation experiences of LGBTQI+ stroke survivors (n=18) and their partners (n=5), revealing themes of sexuality being addressed or absent post-stroke, and negative interactions with health professionals. The findings suggest limited resources and a need for inclusive communication and training.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Burden of fall-related injury and its predictors among stroke survivors attending comprehensive specialized hospitals in the Amhara Regional State, Ethiopia, 2024: A multicenter prospective study.
item.description: A multicenter cross-sectional study among 269 stroke survivors in Ethiopia found a high prevalence of fall-related injury (79.9%, 95% CI: 75.1-84.4). Age > 65 (AOR=2.670), rural residence (AOR=2.352), and injury during walking and turning (AOR=2.960) were significant predictors.
item.author: PubMed
